title: Frame-rate independent orbit camera rig
purpose: Orbit a three.js camera around a target with goals for radius, angles and target reached by exact exponential smoothing, so motion is identical at any frame rate, with radius and polar limits, pans in the view plane scaled by distance and pixel-exact pointer pans. Use it for viewers, editors and strategy cameras.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: The rig needs no three.js; applyTo sets position, up and lookAt on any three.js camera. Only 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: OrbitCameraRig
exports.signature: new OrbitCameraRig(options); rotate(dAzimuth, dPolar); dolly(factor); pan(dx, dy); panPixels(dx, dy, fovDegrees, viewportHeight); setFromPosition(position, target); snap(); update(dt) -> moving; position() -> [x, y, z]; applyTo(camera); current; goal
exports.summary: Orbit state with goals, exact exponential smoothing and limits.

exports.name: orbitPosition
exports.signature: orbitPosition(target, radius, azimuth, polar) -> [x, y, z]
exports.summary: Point on the sphere in three.js's spherical convention (polar from +Y, azimuth about +Y from +Z).

options.name: target
options.meaning: Point the camera orbits and looks at.

options.name: minPolar
options.meaning: Highest view (keeps away from the pole).

limits: No input handling: wire pointer, wheel and touch events to rotate, dolly and panPixels yourself. Smoothing is first order (exponential), so motion starts at full speed; for a spring with zero initial speed use the smooth damp item. Up is always +Y and the polar limits keep the camera off the poles; there is no free roll or quaternion trackball. Azimuth is unbounded (it never wraps) so smoothing never turns the long way. panPixels is exact at the target's depth only. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run for the demo, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Spherical coordinates with polar angle from +Y
Exact exponential smoothing x = goal + (x - goal) e^(-dt / tau)
View-plane basis from the orbit angles for panning
Pixel to world scale 2 r tan(fov / 2) / height
